summary: Iteration 16 — backend-only re-verification of the iteration_15 HIGH-priority over-dedupe fix in /app/backend/statements.py. Re-ran the developer's 42 tests (test_iteration15_dedupe.py + test_iteration14_upi.py): 42/42 PASS. Added a new 12-test edge-case suite (/app/backend/tests/test_iteration16_dedupe_boundary.py) targeting the verified-vs-possible boundary and legacy docs: 12/12 PASS. Full backend regression across 6 modules (iteration12/13/14/15/16 + finaura_regression): 132 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed. CONFIRMED FIXED: the previously failing TestDoubleCount::test_possible_match_bank_row_behaviour now passes — bank 'TEST15_Zzz Alpha' 1234 (10 Aug) + UPI 'TEST15_Qqq Beta' 1234 (12 Aug) is classified under possible_matches (score 0.6) by /statements/verify AND the bank row is KEPT in /financial/overview (dedupe no longer fires on possible matches). BOUNDARY VERIFIED both at unit level (cross_verify/dedupe_across_sources called directly) and via API: score exactly 0.85 (ref present + 1-day gap) → verified_bank_ids=[bank] and the bank row is deduped; synthetic 0.84 (monkeypatched _match_score) → possible, both rows kept; heuristically reachable sub-threshold scores are only 0.6/0.7/0.75 (0.84 is unreachable through the real heuristic — scores are discrete: 0.6, 0.7, 0.75, 0.85, 0.9, 1.0), all of which keep both rows. LEGACY EDGE CASE VERIFIED: a transaction doc inserted with only Mongo _id (no `id` field) does not 500 /statements/verify or /financial/overview — both return 200, the pair is skipped by the matcher and both rows survive analytics with no _id leaked. REGRESSIONS VERIFIED: verified matches with 0-1 day gap still dedupe to exactly one (upi) row; amount-mismatch / type-mismatch / >3-day-gap pairs both kept; bank-only data is a no-op (two identical ₹111 rows preserved); /statements/verify returns verified_matches + possible_matches + upi_only + bank_only + counts + months and leaks NEITHER matched_bank_ids NOR verified_bank_ids, with no _id/user_id/created_at/verified_at on any bank_txn/upi_txn/upi_only/bank_only entry; month scoping still works (bogus month → 0/0); resolve-duplicate 422 (empty body / missing keep_id / missing drop_id), 400 (keep==drop), 404 for either bogus id with the valid side NOT deleted, 200 happy path (bank side deleted, UPI tagged verified=true, overview shows one row), 401/403 unauthenticated. Prior features re-confirmed green via the existing suites: goals CRUD/reorder/priority, whatif purchase + subscription, digital twin, settings preferences, /auth/google/start 302 to accounts.google.com, /auth/me picture, statements preview/parse/confirm-import for bank and upi sources, public /demo/overview. No backend 500s in supervisor logs during the run. NO new product bugs found. One test-infrastructure defect found and fixed by me (details below).

minor.issue: PERF (not a failure): dedupe_across_sources() runs the full O(bank x upi) cross_verify() matcher on every overview request over up to 5000 fetched transactions. Fine at current data volumes, but worth memoising or bounding by month once a user has thousands of rows.

DESIGN (not a failure): matching is greedy in UPI-list order — the first UPI row claims the best available bank row, so a later UPI row that would have been a stronger (ref-based) match for that same bank row is downgraded to bank_only/possible. Verified one UPI can never consume two bank rows, so no double-drop risk; just sub-optimal pairing when several same-amount rows cluster within 3 days.

Legacy docs without an `id` field can never be resolved through this endpoint (lookup is by `id`, so they always 404). Harmless today because the matcher also skips them, but they are permanently un-dedupable.

critical_code_review_comments: dedupe_across_sources() correctly consumes verified_bank_ids only — good. Consider renaming matched_bank_ids to matched_bank_ids_for_review (or dropping it entirely) since it is now used solely to compute bank_only; leaving both similarly-named sets in cross_verify() invites re-introducing the exact 0.6-0.85 over-dedupe bug.

/statements/verify pops both matched_bank_ids and verified_bank_ids defensively — verified no leak. Long term, return a typed Pydantic response model so internal fields cannot leak by omission of a pop().

Legacy docs with no `id` are silently skipped by the matcher. Consider a one-off backfill migration adding uuid `id` to finaura_transactions docs missing it, so those rows participate in dedupe/resolve instead of being invisible to both.
seed_data_creation: All test transactions inserted directly into finaura_transactions for testuser@finaura.dev with TEST15_/TEST16_ description prefixes and purged by autouse fixtures. Verified 0 leftover TEST_/TEST15_/TEST16_ rows after the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: IMPORTANT test-infra note: test_iteration15_dedupe.py and test_iteration16_dedupe_boundary.py assert on hardcoded amounts/dates against one shared preview backend and one shared user, while pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope. Running them under xdist previously produced random failures (1-6 flaky failures per run) because two workers purged/inserted the same TEST15_ rows concurrently, and because iteration15's 'Gym Pro' fixture used the exact same amount (1500) and dates (11/12 Aug 2026) as iteration14's imported CSV row. I fixed both: (a) iteration15 Gym Pro data moved to 1507 on 21/22 Aug 2026, (b) the autouse clean_around fixture in both modules now takes an exclusive fcntl file lock (/tmp/finaura_dedupe_tests.lock) so the dedupe tests are mutually exclusive across workers. Three consecutive parallel runs of 54 tests were green afterwards. If you add more dedupe tests, reuse that lock fixture and pick amounts/dates not used by other modules. Score values reachable by the real heuristic are only 0.6/0.7/0.75/0.85/0.9/1.0 — use monkeypatch on statements._match_score for arbitrary boundary values (note: patch the module attribute, cross_verify resolves it at call time).
rca_of_the_issue: Original iteration_15 bug: cross_verify() put both verified (>=0.85) and possible (0.6-0.85) matches into matched_bank_ids, and dedupe_across_sources() dropped every id in that set, so two unrelated same-amount transactions within 3 days silently lost the bank row from /financial/overview. Fix under test adds a separate verified_bank_ids set (only >=0.85) that dedupe_across_sources consumes, and uses t.get('id') so legacy docs without an id are skipped instead of raising KeyError. Both behaviours confirmed by unit tests on the pure functions and by end-to-end API assertions; the boundary is inclusive at 0.85 and exclusive below it. Secondary (test-only) root cause of the flaky run I observed: shared-state collisions between xdist workers, fixed with a file-lock mutex plus unique fixture amounts — no application code was changed by me.
